items.title: [ag-psd] ag-psd can exhaust memory when parsing crafted PSD dimensions
items.summary: SummaryreadPsd() commits the image/layer buffers from the declared header geometry (width x height x channels x depth, and per-layer rectangles) before validating those values against the actual data. A tiny crafted PSD declaring huge geometry forces a multi-gigabyte allocation.ImpactOn ag-psd 30.2.0, Node 24, a 52-byte PSD makes readPsd(buf) commit ~3.17 GB (measured peak RSS) in ~0.45 s before throwing a catchable RangeError ("Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView") — about 61,000,000x amplification. Because the buffer is committed before validation, the allocation OOM-kills the process before the error on essentially any host (uncatchable), and concurrent requests exhaust memory. Any service reading untrusted PSDs with ag-psd is exposed to a remote DoS.This is distinct from #39 and #206, which involve genuinely large PSDs (memory proportional to real data). Here the input is 52 bytes: the file declares enormous geometry that is never present, so the allocation is driven by an unvalidated header field, not by actual content, an uncontrolled-allocation denial-of-service vulnerability, not proportional memory use.Steps to reproduceThe PoC is a 52-byte PSD (sha256 a1146a6fabdfef289472f99a56851249e7a46e8d19d4d8bf85fe833e2f0158b6). Reconstruct with:base64 -d > poc.psd <<'EOF'OEJQUwABAAAAAAAAAA0AADcuAAA58wAgAAMAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAdEgNZv+i9bc9ygd2A==EOFThen (commits ~3.17 GB before throwing a catchable RangeError):const { readPsd } = require('ag-psd');const buf = require('fs').readFileSync('poc.psd');readPsd(buf.buffer.slice(buf.byteOffset, buf.byteOffset + buf.byteLength));Root causepsdReader.js sizes the off-heap typed-array buffers from the declared header dimensions (and per-layer rectangles, a second independent lever) before validating against the available bytes.Suggested fixValidate the declared dimensions, channel count, depth, and per-layer rectangles against the actual input length (and a sane maximum) before allocating.Referenceshttps://github.com/Agamnentzar/ag-psd/security/advisories/GHSA-qfx6-q44v-9qqwhttps://github.com/Agamnentzar/ag-psd/commit/2d7da68400990bae8ba248a065eb45021fa8000ahttps://github.com/Agamnentzar/ag-psd/blob/2d7da68400990bae8ba248a065eb45021fa8000a/CHANGELOG.mdhttps://github.com/Agamnentzar/ag-psd/tree/31.0.0https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-62297https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qfx6-q44v-9qqw

items.title: [@nuxt/nitro-server] Nuxt: Incomplete fix for GHSA-9v7c-q64q-vv33: a leading `//` in the request path bypasses `server/middleware` path checks and server route rules on page routes
items.summary: SummarySince 4.6.0, Nuxt parses a request path that starts with // as a URL with a host before rendering a page, so //x/admin renders the page at /admin. Nitro's routing, Nitro's route rules and server/middleware see the path as //x/admin, so server-side checks keyed on /admin do not apply. The fix for GHSA-9v7c-q64q-vv33 in 4.6.3 covered dot segments but not this form.ImpactAn unauthenticated attacker can bypass server-side controls that match on the request path of a page route.A route-scoped server handler is skipped:// nuxt.config.tsexport default defineNuxtConfig({  serverHandlers: [{ route: '/admin', middleware: true, handler: '~~/server/admin-guard.ts' }],})// server/admin-guard.tsexport default defineEventHandler((event) => {  if (!isAuthenticated(event)) {    throw createError({ statusCode: 401 })  }})With this handler, /admin returns 401, but //x/admin and ///x/admin render app/pages/admin.vue along with the data it fetches during server rendering. server/middleware that checks event.path.startsWith('/admin') is skipped in the same way.Server-side redirect and headers route rules are also skipped, so '/admin/**': { redirect: '/login' } does not redirect //x/admin/secret, and per-route security headers such as Content-Security-Policy are not sent.Browsers send a path such as //x/admin as written, so a plain link is enough to reach the page.Not affected:API handlers in server/api and server/routes, which Nitro does not match for these paths.appMiddleware route rules and middleware declared with definePageMeta, which are matched against the resolved route.Nuxt 3.x and 4.0.0 to 4.5.x, which pass the path to the page router unchanged, so these requests 404.PatchesFixed in @nuxt/nitro-server@4.6.4, which nuxt@4.6.4 depends on. The renderer now uses the request path exactly as Nitro matched it, so a path starting with // no longer resolves to a different page.WorkaroundsReject request paths that start with // in a server middleware:// server/middleware/double-slash.tsexport default defineEventHandler((event) => {  if (event.path.startsWith('//')) {    throw createError({ statusCode: 404 })  }})A reverse proxy or CDN that merges repeated slashes before forwarding the request also removes the mismatch.CreditsNuxt thanks @kq5y for reporting this issue.Referenceshttps://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/security/advisories/GHSA-r99w-jh2x-3mg9https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-128077https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/commit/75c12c6fb4c22ec2cbde0051da24776d2dffa868https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/releases/tag/v4.6.4https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r99w-jh2x-3mg9

items.title: [@opentelemetry/instrumentation-http] OpenTelemetry JavaScript: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File and Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in @opentelemetry/instrumentation-http
items.summary: Summary@opentelemetry/instrumentation-http redacts sensitive URL query parameters on outgoing (client) spans but not on incoming (server) spans. The server-span path writes the raw query string verbatim into the url.query attribute, so credentials embedded in inbound request URLs — AWS presigned-URL signatures, Azure SAS tokens (sig), GCS signed-URL signatures — are exported in plaintext to the configured tracing backend.Configuring the redactedQueryParams option does not change this, as this applies only to outgoing (client) spans.ImpactInformation disclosure / credential leakage (CWE-200; CWE-532, insertion of sensitive information into telemetry data).Who is impacted: any Node.js service instrumented with @opentelemetry/instrumentation-http — directly or transitively via @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node — that receives inbound requests carrying credentials in the query string. Common cases: services fronting presigned S3/GCS downloads, Azure SAS-token URLs, and signature-authenticated webhooks.Consequence: clients' still-valid credentials are written into server spans and stored by the tracing backend, readable by anyone with span-read access — observability vendor infrastructure, dashboard users, and internal audiences far broader than the credential's intended scope. Presigned-URL signatures typically remain valid for minutes to days after capture, so this is not merely historical exposure.Severity: Moderate. Exploitation requires read access to the telemetry backend, and inbound URLs must actually carry signed credentials. However, the gap is a documented mitigation that silently fails to apply, which defeats the mitigation operators would reach for.PatchesThis vulnerability has been patched in @opentelemetry/instrumentation-http version 0.222.0.Known sensitive query string values (as defined by Semantic Conventions) are redacted by default from span data for incoming spans.The redactedQueryParamsServer configuration option was added for customization.Referenceshttps://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/security/advisories/GHSA-3v2p-hm54-8qcqhttps://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/commit/e086dec7f9304107ef6d50b5877be88895c06aa7https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/releases/tag/experimental/v0.222.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3v2p-hm54-8qcq

items.title: [astro] Astro: XSS via attribute injection in dynamic tag names
items.summary: SummaryWhen a dynamic tag (const Tag = ...; ) resolves to a string, Astro renders it as a raw HTML element name. The name was filtered to remove characters that could inject attributes, but the filter did not handle /. Because HTML parsers treat / inside a tag as an attribute separator, a tag name such as img/src/onerror=alert(1) was rendered as an element with an onerror attribute. The JSX renderer used for MDX did not filter string tag names at all.For example:---const Tag = Astro.url.searchParams.get('as') ?? 'div';---hellorendered ?as=img/src/onerror=alert(1) as live HTML.ImpactReflected or stored cross-site scripting, but only in applications that use untrusted input (such as a request parameter or an uncontrolled CMS field) as all or part of an element name. Astro itself never derives element names from request data.Applications that let content choose an element should map that input to a fixed set of known tags. Letting untrusted input choose an element name is unsafe even with a correct filter, because it can still select elements such as script or iframe.Affected versionsastro <= 7.4.4.PatchesFixed in astro 7.4.5. String tag names in .astro dynamic tags, JSX, and MDX now render only the leading valid element name, so characters such as / or = can no longer change the generated markup. Strings that do not start with a valid element name now throw an error.WorkaroundsUpgrade to astro 7.4.5 or later. Before upgrading, do not use untrusted input as an element name, or map it to a fixed set of known tags.CreditsReported by @uttej-badwane.Referenceshttps://github.com/withastro/astro/security/advisories/GHSA-mh32-jxcr-mh9fhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-126361https://github.com/withastro/astro/pull/18520https://github.com/withastro/astro/commit/e023abac912d7cb6af2b9fb5107ef5dabc667096https://github.com/withastro/astro/releases/tag/astro@7.4.5https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mh32-jxcr-mh9f

items.title: [@astrojs/node] Astro: Image endpoint in @astrojs/node can read files from a case-variant sibling of the output directory on case-sensitive filesystems
items.summary: SummaryThe /_image endpoint used by the @astrojs/node adapter checks that a requested local image is inside the build output directory before reading it from disk. That check compared paths case-insensitively. On case-sensitive filesystems (such as Linux), a directory whose path differs from the output directory only by letter case is a different directory, but it passed the check.For example, with the client output directory at /srv/app/dist/client/, a request such as:/_image?href=/../../DIST/client/secret.png&w=32&f=pngresolved to /srv/app/DIST/client/secret.png and was served, even though that file is outside the output directory.ImpactAn unauthenticated attacker can read image files from outside the output directory, but only when all of the following are true:The site uses on-demand rendering with the @astrojs/node adapter.The server runs on a case-sensitive filesystem.A directory exists whose path matches the output directory except for letter case (for example DIST/client next to dist/client). Such a layout is unusual, and the attacker cannot create it.Only files the image service accepts can be read. Raster images are returned after resizing; SVG files are returned unchanged. Other file types fail during processing. Plain path traversal outside the output directory (for example /../../secret.png) was already rejected and is not affected.Affected versionsastro >= 5.14.3, <= 7.4.6, when used with @astrojs/node (all versions up to 11.1.11). The vulnerable image endpoint is provided by astro and used by the @astrojs/node adapter.PatchesFixed in astro 7.4.7. The path check now compares paths exactly, and only ignores letter case for Windows drive-letter paths. The fix ships in astro, so upgrading @astrojs/node alone is not enough.WorkaroundsUpgrade to astro 7.4.7 or later. Before upgrading, make sure no directory next to the build output directory has a path that differs from it only by letter case.CreditsReported by @zachariah-mithani.Referenceshttps://github.com/withastro/astro/security/advisories/GHSA-r3h5-4585-7x3whttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-126364https://github.com/withastro/astro/commit/7da442bb286e0c29e1c9e1add6727b7cbf434f1ahttps://github.com/withastro/astro/releases/tag/astro@7.4.7https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r3h5-4585-7x3w
